notes.title: Major Update: Original text-heavy and Visualized modes now available
notes.notes:
Fellow vampires! With the latest patch now live, players have a choice of which mode of the game to play.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079568/27d0744f31ca9426bfbe39815e907f3851898e1f.png"]

Those you care about, you let them eat.

Original/Textual: The Original version of the game in which combat and feeding were based on narrative choices, with the game play following a presentation similar to what a game master would narrate. This mode is recommended for new players and for those who want to experience the narration in full, at all stages.



Original/Abbreviated: Same as the Original version of the game in which combat and feeding were based on narrative choices, but with the following change: once a situation has been encountered and described, the next time the same situation occurs, the narration is substituted by a short notification of the outcome.  There is somewhat less reading and clicking but at the cost of no longer being able to see a description again.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079568/6e388cc08758e727251e10cd9b59b018332300e5.png"]



Once in Original mode, you can ask the fortune teller to switch between Textual and Abbreviated.



Alternative: The Alternative version replaces feeding and combat with interactive elements. Hunting and feeding take faster and the combat rules are different, even though the game balance is similar. 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079568/f8b5b0ebeb070efa5f49115b165f500147bf103e.gif"]

In all modes, the game is balanced to be beatable with a character above level 5.  The combat perks that appear at levels 4 and higher in the Alternative version are different from those in the Original, offering new strategies.  Nevertheless, you still need them to have a chance in combat. Having a knife on you still affects one attack in the Original version and offers no combat bonuses in the Alternative. All quests remain unchanged. 



The Alternative mode can be treated as a separate game with the same story and additional assets.

notes.title: Changes are coming
notes.notes:
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45079568/27d0744f31ca9426bfbe39815e907f3851898e1f.png

When I began working on Vampirii, my idea was to recreate the experience of a tabletop game where players sit and let the game master lead the narrative with intriguing descriptions, relying on dice rolls only here and there. Believe it or not, the original idea was that even the combat scenes would be entirely narrated. Of course, this didn't happen, and instead, Vampirii settled on a middle ground. Player feedback and experience, however, suggest that narration, or menu-based encounters, do not suffice. 

For this reason, to make the game loop in Vampirii more enjoyable and allow players to experience its unique story with all of its branches, the following changes are underway:

Combat Overhaul: Despite all the work that went into the current system, including the secret battles (which of you has fought other vampires in Oswald?), Vampirii's combat will change from being based on menu choices to an interactive one. You will be able to select which opponent to attack, and at the end of the turn, your opponents will fight and fire back. Human opponents will use their fists, knives, rifles, etc., to hurt your blood pool. They will drop loot dynamically, so there will be no more battle recaps.

As a consequence, the combat perks will be changed. One will improve your fang attack, while another will give you a one-time advantage for each encounter. This will lead to changes in balance, but the goal is to keep the game difficulty roughly the same.

Breaking and Entering Overhaul: Similar to the combat overhaul, the breaking and entering portion of feeding will change from being based on menu choices to an interactive one. Outdoor hunting for game, although already fast and rewarding, will receive the same treatment as combat.

When?: This will be ready by mid-April, probably sooner.

notes.title: Version 1.1
notes.notes:
Changes to hunting and feeding feedback

* When facing a situation for the first time while prowling residential areas, the player will see the full text describing the scene and the outcome of any action chosen. When the same situation occurs again later, the description will be omitted (unless it is very short) and the outcome will be presented either directly by loading the next portion or in a very short message that indicates the outcome. For example, when trying to enter a home through the window after a scenario has already been experienced, a successful outcome will bring the inside content right away and a negative outcome will bring a message, such as "it doesn't open."

* Also, the comments before and after feeding were removed, expect for the very first instances. While they will be missed, these comments ran the risk of becoming repetitive and simply resulting in having to click extra times. If players desire that comments come back in some form, they may be made a randomized rare occurrence.

The final and fastest feeding grounds do not involve entering and breaking and thus received no changes. These are already "fast enough" in both leveling and sustenance.

Happy hunting!

notes.title: Vampirii 1.1: Changes in Hunting and Feeding feedback
notes.notes:
What is new in Version 1.1? Changes and the reasons behind them.

https://clan.cloudflare.steamstatic.com/images/45079568/27d0744f31ca9426bfbe39815e907f3851898e1f.png

Fellow vampires,

The "hunt and feed" cycle before "getting out of town" in Vampirii faces a challenge when it comes to meeting two goals at once: 

* providing a narrative experience that approximates that of a table top game with some unnecessary complexities removed;  and
*  keeping the pace of the game such that players can spend enough time to feel both immersed and invested in the story and the character's "life" as a vampire, but not so much time that a mechanic would become to feel repetitive. 

Hunting and feeding are both core mechanics that balance the rest of the questing, provide the fuel for leveling up and fighting, and keep our character grounded in reality regarding his new existence.   

Depending on the life story background, the player faces different options and chances of success when negotiating windows, garage doors, roofs, and places where keys might be hidden.  While the narrative pool of scenarios and outcomes offers enough variety (including 1/20 and 1/10 occurrences while attempting to beak in), sooner or later a player has seen all the outcomes.

To address this issue, the following changes were made:

* When facing a situation for the first time while prowling residential areas, the player will see the full text describing the scene and the outcome of any action chosen.  When the same situation occurs again later, the description will be omitted (unless it is very short) and the outcome will be presented either directly by loading the next portion or in a very short message that indicates the outcome.  For example, when trying to enter a home through the window after a scenario has already been experienced, a successful outcome will bring the inside content right away and a negative outcome will bring a message, such as "it doesn't open." 

* Also, the comments before and after feeding were removed, expect for the very first instances. While they will be missed, these comments ran the risk of becoming repetitive and simply resulting in having to click extra times. If players desire that comments come back in some form, they may be made a randomized rare occurrence.
 
The final and fastest feeding grounds do not involve entering and breaking and thus received no changes. These are already "fast enough" in both leveling and sustenance. 

Happy hunting!
